author: TEDx Talks
description:
An estimated quarter-million patients die from medical errors in the United States each year—and one of the deadliest is a wound many people barely understand: pressure injuries, or bedsores, which are associated with more American deaths than motor-vehicle crashes. Martin Burns shows how his team learned to measure the invisible biology beneath the skin before damage becomes visible, turning a coin-toss skin assessment into a system shown to prevent up to 93% of these wounds. Change what people can see, and you change what they do—allowing caregivers to act before hidden damage becomes an open wound.

Martin Burns has spent 15 years working to make preventable patient harm visible and stoppable before it happens. His work is driven by a personal intolerance for avoidable human suffering and a belief that better information can help healthcare systems act earlier, make better decisions, and protect the safety and dignity of the people in their care. Greece has a strong cultural legacy, but while its ancient past continues to define its image, its contemporary identity remains largely untold. This talk explores how cinema can become a tool of cultural diplomacy and a strategic investment, allowing Greece to share its modern stories, support its creators, and strengthen its presence on the global stage.

Because when a country does not tell its own stories, others will tell them instead. Greece does not need only to preserve its past, it needs to narrate its present and imagine its future.

description:
Adaleti çoğu zaman yalnızca gerçekler üzerinden değerlendirdiğimizi düşünürüz. Peki aynı gerçeklere bakan insanlar neden bambaşka sonuçlara ulaşabiliyor? Münazara deneyimlerim ve hukuk alanındaki hedeflerim bana, adaletin yalnızca kurallardan değil, aynı zamanda bakış açısından da beslendiğini gösterdi. Bu konuşmada, farklı perspektifleri anlamanın neden gerçek adaletin vazgeçilmez bir parçası olduğunu anlatıyorum.

We often think justice is determined solely by facts. But if the facts are the same, why do people reach completely different conclusions? Through my experience in competitive debate and my passion for law, I discovered that justice is shaped not only by rules but also by perspective. In this talk, I explore why understanding different viewpoints is essential to achieving true justice. Ayşe Tuana Akıncı, TED Bodrum Koleji mezunu olup Fordham University International Studies bölümüne %75 başarı bursuyla kabul edilmiştir. Uluslararası ilişkiler ve küresel diplomasi alanların
title: Adalet Bakış Açısıyla Başlar | Ayşe Tuana Akıncı | TEDxBodrum College Youth
